units.passage: Faculty may wish to allow students to use generative AI tools, provide specific parameters for its use, or prohibit its use for course assignments and assessments
units.policy: Faculty may allow generative AI, provide specific parameters for its use, or prohibit its use for course assignments and assessments.
units.why: The sentence lists three options for faculty ("allow", "provide specific parameters", "prohibit"), so the page sets no single rule and leaves the choice to each instructor; P04 fits because the decision is per instructor.

units.passage: Artificial intelligence (AI) language models, such as ChatGPT, may be used for [assignment types A, B & C] with appropriate citation, but not for [assignment types D, E & F].
units.policy: In the quoted Minnesota sample, AI language models may be used for some assignment types with appropriate citation, but not for others.
units.why: Quoted Minnesota template: AI "may be used for [assignment types A, B & C] with appropriate citation, but not for [assignment types D, E & F]" sets per-assignment permission with citation, P04 (assignment-level rule).
units.fit_note: Also requires citation for the permitted assignment types.

units.passage: Some instructors may not allow AI-generated content in assignments, or they may have specific rules about how it is used.
units.policy: Some instructors may not allow AI-generated content in assignments, or they may have specific rules about how it is used.

units.passage: Instructors have the flexibility to set their own course-specific policies regarding the allowable use of generative AI in coursework.
units.why: 'Instructors have the flexibility to set their own course-specific policies regarding the allowable use of generative AI' places the decision with each instructor, so P04, addressed to instructors.

units.passage: Whether you decide to encourage the use of Generative AI in your course, permit its use for specific assignments, or prohibit the use of it entirely,

units.fit_note: Names three options (encourage, permit for specific assignments, prohibit) without defining them as tiers.

units.passage: Ultimately, this committee leaves instructors to set their own course policies regarding student use of generative AI.
units.why: 'this committee leaves instructors to set their own course policies regarding student use of generative AI': delegation to instructors, P04.

units.passage: Individual assignments and exams may have additional, specific requirements related to original work which should be clearly defined by the instructor.
units.why: 'Individual assignments and exams may have additional, specific requirements related to original work which should be clearly defined by the instructor' lets assignments set their own rules: P04.
units.fit_note: Concerns assignment- and exam-level requirements on original work.

units.passage: Considering this, we suggest that rather than focusing solely on ChatGPT, instructors should instead focus on what role they would like all generative AI tools to play in their classes and in their students' work going forward. How might instructors approach student use of generative AI? We suggest that there are two ways instructors can approach student use of generative AI:
units.why: Instructors 'should instead focus on what role they would like all generative AI tools to play in their classes': the role is decided per instructor, P04.

units.passage: Within the overlapping frameworks of academic freedom, course coordination, and department/unit curriculum and policies, instructors set expectations for their classes, and these expectations can differ.
units.policy: Within the overlapping frameworks of academic freedom, course coordination, and department/unit curriculum and policies, instructors set expectations for their classes, and these expectations can differ.
units.why: 'instructors set expectations for their classes, and these expectations can differ' places the decision with each instructor, bounded by academic freedom, course coordination and department policy. This is P04; the stance of the whole document is therefore delegates.

units.passage: (ii) use of or referral to sources beyond those authorized by the instructor in writing papers, preparing reports, solving problems, or carrying out other assignments;
units.why: Cheating includes 'sources beyond those authorized by the instructor in writing' for assignments, so the instructor decides which aids are allowed; this is instructor-set authorization (P04), and by default unauthorized sources are barred.
units.fit_note: Generic sources rule, not AI-specific; also implies a restrictive default unless the instructor authorizes.

units.passage: The term unauthorized use of artificially generated content, includes, but is not limited to: (i) use of artificial intelligence tools or other tools that generate artificial content in taking quizzes, tests, examinations, or other assessments without permission from the instructor; (ii) submitting work for evaluation as one’s own that was produced in material or substantial part through use of artificial intelligence tools or other tools that generate artificial content without permission from the instructor; (iii) using artificial intelligence tools or other tools that generate artificial content in a manner contrary to instructions from the instructor; or (iv) using artificial intelligence tools or other tools that generate artificial content in a manner that violates any other provision of these rules concerning academic dishonesty.
units.why: Using AI 'in a manner contrary to instructions from the instructor' is misconduct, so the instructor's instructions set the AI rule, which is per-instructor control (P04).

units.passage: Therefore, it is the instructor’s prerogative to allow or prohibit the use of any generative AI tool.
units.why: The memo says "it is the instructor’s prerogative to allow or prohibit the use of any generative AI tool", so the university sets no rule and hands the decision to instructors; P04 fits and P85 does not because it is about instructors, not units.

units.passage: You may discover that if you allow students to engage with generative AI, specific guidelines may need to accompany each assignment.
units.why: "specific guidelines may need to accompany each assignment" says the rule may be set per assignment, so P04 (per-assignment rule).

units.passage: WSU recognizes that additional policies may be preferred by some, including explicit encouragement of students using AI.
units.why: "WSU recognizes that additional policies may be preferred by some, including explicit encouragement" leaves room for policies beyond the four; instructor-level choice, P04.

units.passage: Faculty need to decide whether AI can be used as a supplement, teaching, or support tool for their students.

units.passage: Will you allow students to use AI to help them with assignments? Within what parameters?

units.passage: Selling, giving, offering, or stealing all or part of a test or term paper or any other academic assignment or course materials, unauthorized use of resources, enlisting in the assistance of a substitute when taking exams, destroying another's work, threatening students or instructors, or any other misconduct identified in the course syllabus or other written information.
units.why: 'any other misconduct identified in the course syllabus' lets syllabi define additional misconduct, supporting instructor-set rules (P04).

units.passage: Consequently, the application of the Honor Code in a particular course is left in part to the discretion of the instructor and his/her students.
units.policy: The application of the Honor Code in a particular course is left in part to the discretion of the instructor and his/her students.
units.why: 'the application of the Honor Code in a particular course is left in part to the discretion of the instructor' lets instructors shape the rules per course, which is how the AI permission works; P04, instructor, before-course, informs.

units.passage: Just as a graphing calculator or translation machine may be permissible in certain contexts and inappropriate in others, so too the appropriate use of AI is varied across disciplines and subject matters.

units.passage: A faculty member may prohibit AI in the classroom completely.

units.passage: the subcommittee aligned with the first approach to require faculty to explicitly state how AI can and cannot be used in the classroom without dictating what that looks like for faculty.

units.policy: Some instructors may prohibit any use of digital resources such as generative AI, whereas other instructors may allow it when properly cited.

units.passage: Whether an instructor chooses to discourage, limit, or embrace AI use in their courses, designing course content with AI in mind and communicating a clear message to students is invaluable.

units.why: 'Instructors are free to establish their own additional protocols... including allowing or disallowing some or all use' hands the decision to each instructor (P04), a delegation rather than a university rule.

units.passage: Within each course, instructors at Yale have full authority to determine whether and how students may use AI when completing assignments.

units.passage: How and whether instructors permit you to use AI writing tools at Yale will vary widely from course to course, and is always subject to each instructor’s authority and policy.

units.passage: The colleges neither prohibit AI outright nor require it.

units.passage: The colleges neither prohibit AI outright nor require it. Faculty decide how AI fits the learning goals of their courses, and students are expected to use AI honestly and as their courses allow. What matters is that any use of AI is constructive, reviewed, and disclosed.

units.passage: Give instructors clear authority and practical tools to set AI expectations for their own courses.

units.passage: Where an instructor's stated course policy differs from this document, the instructor's policy controls.

units.passage: Instructors may set stricter or more permissive rules for their own courses and for individual assignments, provided these are clearly stated as described in Section 7.
units.why: "Instructors may set stricter or more permissive rules for their own courses and for individual assignments" gives rule-setting to instructors (P04).

units.passage: Instructors may set different levels for different assignments within the same course.

units.passage: The assignment-level policy belongs on the assignment itself, in a clearly marked section or box that states the applicable level, any assignment-specific conditions, and the consequences of noncompliance (see Appendix B). Stating the policy on each assignment clarifies it and reflects that AI parameters may legitimately change from one assignment to the next within the same course. 7.2 What Students Disclose and Retain Wherever AI use is permitted at UG 1 or above, you must submit a written statement identifying any AI tools or AI-enabled features used and explaining how they were used for the assignment. A structured statement of work is ideal, but any written disclosure satisfies this requirement; what matters is that you put your AI use on the record and stand behind what you report.
units.why: "AI parameters may legitimately change from one assignment to the next within the same course" says rules vary by assignment, P11.
units.fit_note: Applies within one course (assignment to assignment), not across courses.
